q: Weyl's polynomial equidistribution theorem generalises Weyl's rotation theorem. It states that for a polynomial p(n) = αₖnᵏ + … + α₁n + α₀ with at least one αᵢ (i ≥ 1) irrational, the sequence {p(n)} is:
exp: Weyl's theorem (1916): if any non-constant coefficient αᵢ of p(n) is irrational, then {p(n)} = {p(n) mod 1} is equidistributed in [0,1]. Proved by van der Corput's theorem (reducing to lower-degree polynomials) and Weyl sums |Σ e^{2πi p(n)}| = o(N).
